name: veterinary_clinic_system_090_after_hours_message_log
instruction: The answering service took a voicemail from owner 7 (Frank Kowalski) about rescheduling an appointment. Follow the after-hours triage protocol for the episode: (1) log an inbound phone communications row from owner 7 with body 'Requested reschedule of next appointment; called after closing.', subject 'After-hours voicemail <batch_code>', logged_by 'answering service', occurred_at the episode timestamp, and patient_id set to the id of that owner's patient; (2) identify the on-call DVM for that patient's location — the provider whose role is 'veterinarian' and whose location_id matches the patient's location_id — and page them with an outbound communications row to that provider (provider_id set to that provider's id, channel 'sms', direction 'outbound', subject 'After-hours page <batch_code>', body 'Reschedule request from Frank Kowalski (owner 7) for patient <patient name> — please call back.', logged_by 'answering service', occurred_at the episode timestamp, owner_id left empty); (3) create exactly one ops_reports row {report: 'after_hours_triage', batch_code, owner_id: '7', patient_id, on_call_provider_id, triage_note: 'Reschedule request paged to <provider full name>.'}. All identity fields must be derived from live data, not hardcoded.
_max_steps_note: set after live gold measurement in QC session
_par_steps_note: set after live gold measurement in QC session

success_criteria.summary: Two new communications rows (inbound voicemail + outbound page) with exact fields, patient_id and provider_id derived from live owner/patient/provider joins; one ops_reports after_hours_triage row for this batch with correct owner/patient/provider/triage_note; all pre-existing communications and other collections byte-identical.

checks.expect: Two new communications rows and one ops_reports row with fields derived from live data; on-call DVM verified by API-vs-SQL dual path.

hazards: Pre-existing communications rows (160 total) reuse a small set of subjects and bodies (e.g., 'Billing question resolved', 'Discussed dental quote', 'Boarding dates confirmed'); matching the new rows by text alone collides with these decoys — the verifier matches by owner_id/patient_id/provider_id plus the live batch_code.

Owner 7's patient is patient 10 (Willow, equine) with location_id '2' (snapshot row). Provider id 9 (Lucy Tran, groomer) is also at location 2; an agent that picks the first provider at the location without filtering role='veterinarian' will page the wrong person. Provider id 3 (Dr. Priya Natarajan) is the only veterinarian at location 2.

Provider id 1 (Dr. Elena Alvarez, veterinarian) and id 2 (Dr. Marcus Chen, veterinarian) are both at location 1; an agent hardcoding 'first veterinarian' without joining through the patient's location will page the wrong DVM.
The ops_reports collection does not exist in the seed snapshot; gold and verifier must tolerate a missing table on first read and create it on demand.

The communications schema in the snapshot has no patient_id or provider_id columns; the gold must push these foreign keys as extra fields, and the verifier must verify them, or the two new rows cannot be distinguished from the 160 pre-existing decoys.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Fuses a simple message-log create with a multi-hop owner/patient/provider lookup and an audit report, requiring the agent to derive the on-call DVM from live data and produce two distinct communications rows plus one ops_reports row. Existing public benchmarks either log a single row or ask for a hardcoded recipient, not a join-driven triage workflow with provider paging.
